translation: The Blessed Lord said: Once again, O mighty-armed warrior, listen to My supreme, transcendent word! Because you are My dear companion and find joy in My teachings, I unfold this to you out of a deep desire for your ultimate welfare.
Neither the hosts of cosmic powers nor the ancient great sages understand My origin. For I am the primeval source from which all the gods and great sages emerge in every possible way.
He who recognizes Me as unborn, without beginning, and as the absolute Sovereign of all worlds—he alone among mortals is free from delusion, and he is completely liberated from all sins.
Intellect, empirical knowledge, clarity free from delusion, patience, truthfulness, control over the senses, tranquility of mind, happiness, sorrow, birth, death, fear, and courage;
Non-violence, equanimity, contentment, self-discipline, charity, fame, and infamy—all these diverse qualities found within living creatures emanate directly from My cosmic laws.

The seven ancient great sages and the four foundational Manus (the cosmic administrators) emerged directly from My consciousness, born of My mental design. From their lineage have sprouted all the human populations currently populating this world.

He who understands in its true essence this magnificent manifestation (Vibhuti) and My cosmic power (Yoga), becomes integrated in unshakeable, flawless meditation; there is absolutely no doubt about this.

I am the sole source from which the entire cosmos projects; everything moves and operates driven by My underlying law. Realizing this grand truth, the wise, overflowing with deep spiritual emotion, focus their lives entirely upon Me.

With their minds completely saturated by My presence, their very life-currents dedicated to My mission, illuminating one another, and continuously discussing My divine laws, they live in profound contentment and rejoice in spiritual bliss.
To those who are permanently integrated and serve Me with pure, affectionate love, I gladly bestow that internal Yoga of clear discernment (Buddhi-yogam) by which they swiftly ascend to Me.

Out of pure compassion for them, I, residing securely within the core of their consciousness, completely shatter the darkness born of ignorance using the radiant, blazing lamp of realized wisdom (Jnana-dipena bhasvata).
Arjuna said: You are the Supreme Brahman, the ultimate Abode, the holy Purifier! All the cosmic seers declare You to be the eternal, divine, primordial Person, unborn and all- pervading.
Thus have you been celebrated by all the great sages—by the divine seer Narada, by Asita, Devala, and the great Vyasa. And now, You are declaring this truth directly to me Yourself.

I accept everything that You have just declared to me as absolute, unassailable truth, O Keshava! Neither the cosmic powers nor the demonic forces, O Blessed Lord, can fully comprehend the depth of Your divine manifestation.
You alone know Your infinite self by the light of Your own divine consciousness, O Supreme Person, Creator of all entities, Lord of all creation, God of all gods, and sovereign Ruler of the universe!
Kindly recount to me in complete, exhaustive detail Your radiant, divine manifestations (divyah atma-vibhutayah), by which concentrated splendors You pervade and sustain all these worlds.

How can I continuously meditate upon You, O Master of Yoga, so that I may acquire absolute knowledge of Your presence? In which specific objects, variables, or forms of nature, O Blessed Lord, should You be contemplated by me?

Recount to me once more in expansive detail Your cosmic powers (Yoga) and Your manifestations (Vibhuti), O Janardana! For I can never tire of listening to Your life-giving, nectar-like words; my thirst for this wisdom is insatiable.

The Blessed Lord said: Very well, O best of the Kuru clan! I shall unfold to you My radiant, divine manifestations, focusing exclusively on the pre-eminent categories (pradhanyatah). For there is absolutely no end or boundary to the exhaustive expansion of My cosmic attributes.

I am the inner Self (Atma), O Gudakesha (Arjuna), residing permanently seated within the core heart of every single living creature. I am the absolute Beginning, the middle Existence, and the ultimate End of all entities.
simple_explanation: This is the ultimate, foundational Vibhuti. If you want to locate God, do not run away to look behind distant clouds. Look at the conscious pulse operating inside your own heart and inside the hearts of your fellow human beings. God is the underlying reality that allows consciousness to observe nature.

translation: Among the twelve solar deities (Adityas), I am Vishnu; among radiant lights, I am the blazing, sun; among the storm-gods, I am Marichi; and among the nocturnal stars, I am the glowing moon.

Among the Vedas, I am the Samaveda (the Veda of structural melody); among the cosmic powers, I am Indra (Vasava); among the human senses, I am the processing mind; and within all living creatures, I am the living pulse of consciousness (Chetana).

Among the tear-striking forces (Rudras), I am Shankara; among the guardians of material wealth, I am Kubera (Vittesha); among the foundational elements (Vasus), I am the purifying fire; and among the peaked mountains, I am the central mount Meru.

Among the royal mentors and counselors, know Me, O Partha, to be the pre-eminent Brihaspati; among military commanders, I am Skanda (the lord of strategic war); and among reservoirs of water, I am the boundless ocean (sagarah).

Among the great ancient sages, I am Bhrigu; among vocal utterances, I am the single monosyllabic word Om; among sacrifices, I am the non-violent sacrifice of quiet contemplation (Japa-yajna); and among unmoving, static monuments, I am the majestic Himalaya.
simple_explanation: Why is Japa-yajna designated as the pre-eminent sacrifice? Material sacrifices involve gathering physical resources, friction, and occasionally the disruption of smaller elements. But Japa-yajna—the internal, steady chanting and contemplation of divine laws—demands no external capital and hurts no living creature. It is pure, non-attached mental refinement.

translation: Among all the trees of the earth, I am the sacred Ashvattha (the banyan tree, symbolic of the universe); among divine seers, I am Narada; among celestial singers, I am Chitraratha; and among perfected thinkers, I am the analytical sage Kapila (the author of Sankhya philosophy).
Among royal stallions, know Me to be Uchchaishrava, emerged from the churn of immortality; among grand elephants, know Me as Airavata; and among human beings, I am the sovereign king (naradhipam).

Among striking weapons, I am the lightning bolt (Vajra); among cows, I am the wish- yielding Kamadhuk; among generative causes, I am the force of procreative love (Kandarpa); and among striking serpents, I am Vasuki.
Among deep-water serpents, I am Ananta; among aquatic lords, I am Varuna; among ancestral guardians, I am Aryama; and among evaluating regulators who enforce justice, I am Yama (the lord of death).

Among the Titan clans (Daityas), I am the dedicated Prahlada; among measures and calculators, I am inexorable Time (Kalah); among beasts, I am the majestic lion (mrigendrah); and among wings, I am Garuda (Vainateya).

Among purifying forces, I am the sweeping wind; among warriors who wield weapons, I am Rama; among aquatic predators, I am the powerful crocodile; and among flowing rivers, I am the sacred Ganga (Jahnavi).

Of all manifest creations, I am the absolute Beginning, the middle course, and the terminating End, O Arjuna! Among forms of education, I am the science of the inner Self (Adhyatma- vidya); and among structural arguments, I am the objective, truth-seeking logic (Vadah).
simple_explanation: Ancient logical grammar outlines three kinds of debate: Jalpa (debating purely to win by using tricks), Vitanda (destructive criticism without proposing an alternative), and Vada (an honest dialogue where both sides seek the objective truth). Krishna states that He represents Vada. God is located in rational, honest verification, never in toxic sophistry or political screaming.

translation: Among alphabet letters, I am the primary sound 'A' (Akaro-asmi); among grammatical compounds, I am the balanced coordinate compound (Dvandvah); I am inexorable, infinite Time (Akshayah Kalah); and I am the multi-faced Sustainer who looks out everywhere across creation.

I am all-devouring Death that strips away possessions, and I am the generative cause of everything that is yet to come into history. Among feminine virtues, I am fame, prosperity, eloquent speech, retentive memory, sharp intelligence, unswerving fortitude, and patient forgiveness.

Among the vocal melodies of the Samaveda, I am the majestic Brihatsama; among poetic meters, I am the sacred, regular Gayatri; among calendar months, I am the pristine Margashirsha; and among seasons, I am the blossoming spring (Kusumakarah).

Among calculated traps used by deceivers, I am the strategic game of dice; I am the brilliant radiance of the magnificent; I am victory personified; I am systematic enterprise and determination; and I am the pure goodness (Sattvam) within the virtuous.

Among the Vrishni clan, I am Vasudev (Krishna himself); among the Pandava brothers, I am Dhananjaya (Arjuna himself); among the reflective sages, I am the great editor Vyasa; and among visionary poets, I am the sharp counselor Ushanas (Shukracharya).

Among regulatory systems that curb crime, I am the lawful force of punishment (Dandah); among those who seek geopolitical victory, I am ethical statesmanship (Nitih); among secrets, I am the fortress of silence (Maunam); and I am the direct wisdom within the wise.

And whatever is the underlying vital seed of every single living creature, that am I, O Arjuna! For absolutely no moving or unmoving entity can have a footing or exist for a single split- second independent of My presence.

There is absolutely no final end or limit to My radiant, divine manifestations, O scorcher of foes! This expansive list that I have just recounted to you represents a tiny, summary illustration (uddeshatah) of My cosmic attributes.

Whatever entity exists in this universe that is endowed with extraordinary majesty, radiant prosperity, or intense, crushing energy—understand clearly that it has emerged from a mere tiny fraction of My limitless, blinding power (tejomsha-sambhavam).

But of what use is it to you, O Arjuna, to collect an endless, detailed catalogue of these individual attributes? Let it suffice to realize that I support, stabilize, and pervade this entire, boundless universe by a single, infinitesimal fraction of My cosmic Being (ekamshena sthito jagat).
